source.title: A Bayesian Perspective on Training Speed and Model Selection
source.authors: Clare Lyle; Lisa Schut; Binxin Ru; Yarin Gal; Mark van der Wilk

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own experiments relating SGD training-trajectory statistics and model or subnetwork performance to test loss, using FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 DNNs. This conceptually bears on V7's measured-properties version, though its statistic and comparison differ from magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own DNN results linking sum over training losses (SOTL) and ensemble or subnetwork weights with test performance. The paper's linear-model and NTK model-selection results concern marginal likelihood and are not rows for the listed versions. Prior-work statements are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Figures 3 and 7 compare held-out cross-entropy across SGD-trained CNNs and MLPs on FashionMNIST, bearing on V3 in a new image dataset. The supplied text does not reveal the architecture-specific plotted values or establish their ordering. SOTL correlations do not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate but overstates direct evidence for subnetwork generalization. The authors derive marginal-likelihood estimators and ensemble-weight results for linear models and infinite-width networks, then report preliminary DNN evidence linking SOTL to test loss and ensemble weights. Their subnetwork experiments relate weight magnitudes to accumulated classifier cross-entropy; the proposed explanation of SGD's generalization bias remains tentative.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies SOTL and ensemble or subnetwork weights, not random-label fitting, interpolation-width sweeps, or magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.method_sensitivity: Training scheme changes the ensemble-weight relationship: the weight difference is reported as magnified in concurrent training, where the ensemble focuses on CNNs; the authors suggest CNNs learn more easily and get larger weights earlier.

fits_no_version.finding: SOTL correlates with held-out cross-entropy, and architectures with lower individual test error receive higher ensemble weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-trajectory losses predict held-out performance and ensemble weighting for the tested FashionMNIST architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher-weight groups of MLP penultimate-layer nodes have better performance estimated through accumulated classifier cross-entropy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final-layer weight magnitudes track SOTL-based subnetwork performance on FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: The convolutional NTK-GP has higher marginal-likelihood estimates than the fully connected NTK-GP on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bayesian evidence favors the convolutional kernel in this MNIST regression comparison.

record.problems: The DNN evidence is described by the authors as preliminary. Main-text results are primarily qualitative correlations without numerical coefficients or per-architecture values; plotted shaded variability is summarized, but exact values are not stated. The empirical DNN study uses FashionMNIST and the appendix reports CIFAR-10 for subnetworks; the paper does not test the listed versions' interventions or measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Linear-model and infinite-width NTK model-selection experiments report marginal-likelihood estimation or model ranking, not a listed version's outcome.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.

Local-connectivity interventions, learned sparse connections, convolutional initialization of fully connected networks, and classification-error comparisons. The available architecture comparison uses FashionMNIST cross-entropy.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization gaps at matched training loss, and rankings against norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Extract held-out cross-entropy separately for each CNN and MLP under parallel training, including variability and architecture settings. These plotted results permit a direct architecture comparison, but neither the rows nor the supplied figure text gives their values or ordering. No directional V3 verdict can be justified from the available prose.
missing.locator: Section 4.2.1, Figure 3 middle panel; Appendix B.2–B.3, Figure 7 left panel

record.verdict_notes: The architecture-specific plots are not readable from the supplied text. CNN emphasis during concurrent training establishes an optimization preference, not by itself lower held-out error. None of R1–R4 directly records the architecture comparison needed for V3.

versions.untested_parts: Test error as width increases past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, training-loss-matched networks, and comparisons against norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing influential memorized examples and measuring the change in test accuracy.

rows.subject: DNNs (MLPs and CNNs; individual architectures not specified in the text)
rows.size_stated: Varied layers, nodes and kernel sizes; exact values not stated in the main text
rows.operation_detail: Compared SOTL with average test cross-entropy across architectures in parallel training.
rows.measure: Correlation between SOTL (standardized by number of training samples) and average test cross-entropy.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations shown by shaded regions; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: Authors state that the correlation validates that SOTL is correlated with generalization; individual architecture-level values are not stated in the prose.
rows.check: The reported SOTL–test-loss correlation is supported, but measures neither magnitude-aware sharpness nor a direct CNN–MLP performance difference.

rows.subject: DNNs (MLPs and CNNs; individual architectures not specified in the text)
rows.size_stated: Varied layers, nodes and kernel sizes; exact values not stated in the main text
rows.operation_detail: Related linear ensemble weights to the individual models' test errors in concurrent training.
rows.measure: Relationship between test error when models are trained individually and weight assigned by linear ensemble.
rows.value: Architectures with lower individual test error are given higher ensemble weight.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations shown by shaded regions; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative relationship; it does not provide separate numeric values for each architecture.
rows.check: The ensemble-weight relationship is supported, but the aggregated row does not record held-out performance separately for CNNs and MLPs.

rows.subject: MLP network (units 200, 200, 10)
rows.operation_detail: Compared final-layer weights assigned to subnetworks with their SOTL-based performance.
rows.measure: Relationship between assigned subnetwork weight and subnetwork performance estimated by summed cross-entropy.
rows.value: SGD assigns larger weights to subnetworks that perform well.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals estimated over 10 seeds (described as 2σ for both weight and SOTL).
rows.note: The reported relationship is qualitative; the plotted class-specific numerical values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Measures final-layer weight versus accumulated cross-entropy of logistic classifiers on grouped penultimate-layer activations. This is not a listed version's outcome or direct evidence of subnetwork held-out generalization.
